subject: science
title: Plants
description: The functions of the parts of flowering plants, what plants need to grow, how water travels through a plant, and the life cycle from pollination to seed dispersal.

objectives.statement: Identify and describe the functions of different parts of flowering plants: roots, stem/trunk, leaves and flowers.
Explore the requirements of plants for life and growth (air, light, water, nutrients from soil, and room to grow) and how they vary from plant to plant.
Investigate the way in which water is transported within plants.
Explore the part that flowers play in the life cycle of flowering plants, including pollination, seed formation and seed dispersal.

items.prompt: Which part of a plant takes in water and holds the plant in the ground?
Which part of a plant makes food using sunlight?
What is the main job of the stem?
options: to hold the plant up and carry water

items.prompt: Which part of the plant helps it to make seeds?

items.statement: Roots usually grow downwards into the soil.
The leaves hold the plant firmly in the ground.

items.prompt: Name two things a plant needs to grow well.
items.answer: Any two of: light, water, air, nutrients from soil, room to grow

items.prompt: Which of these do plants get from the soil?

items.statement: A plant kept in a dark cupboard with no light will grow just as well as one on a sunny windowsill.
Different plants can need different amounts of water and light.

items.prompt: A class grows two identical plants. One is given water and the other is not. Everything else is kept the same. What is this test finding out?
options: how tall the plant can grow

items.prompt: How does water get from the soil to the leaves of a plant?
items.answer: It is taken in by the roots and travels up through the stem
acceptableAnswers: up the stem from the roots

items.statement: Water travels up a plant through the stem.

items.prompt: A white flower is placed in water dyed blue. After a day the petals turn blue. What does this show?
options: flowers can change colour on their own
water travels up the stem into the flower

items.statement: Plants lose some water from their leaves into the air.

items.prompt: What is it called when pollen is carried from one flower to another?
Which of these often helps to carry pollen between flowers?
Put these stages in the correct order.
options: pollination → seed formation → seed dispersal → new plant grows
seed dispersal → pollination → new plant grows → seed formation
new plant grows → pollination → seed dispersal → seed formation

items.prompt: Why is it useful for seeds to be spread far away from the parent plant?
items.answer: So the new plants have space, light and water and do not have to compete with the parent plant
acceptableAnswers: so they have room to grow
so they don't compete for light and water

items.statement: Some seeds are spread by the wind.
Seed dispersal means the seed turning into a flower while still inside the parent plant.
